title: LLM Engineer
summary: An engineer who turns language-model behavior into explicit, measurable, adaptable, and operable systems while preserving evidence and authority boundaries.

includes: Define language-task contracts and engineer prompts, context, retrieval, structured output, evaluation, adaptation, and inference evidence.
Diagnose language-model-system behavior across managed and open-weight paths and preserve behavior-facing release and change gates.
Prepare technical evidence and limitations while routing product, domain, legal, privacy, security, safety, platform, and formal decisions to named authorities.
excludes: Set product priority, domain truth, legal or licensing interpretation, privacy approval, security architecture, or formal safety and risk acceptance.
Own shared MLOps and platform infrastructure, frontier model research, customer-embedded delivery, or autonomous-agent orchestration by default.
Treat a fluent response, benchmark, model card, schema, or operational metric as sufficient proof of product fitness.

competencies.title: Language tasks and behavior contracts
competencies.description: Specify language tasks, consequences, states, limits, and authority as measurable contracts.

objectives.statement: Define task, consequence, output, uncertainty, non-goals, abstention, escalation, authority, and measurable claims.

competencies.title: Transformer and token literacy
competencies.description: Use model mechanisms at engineering depth without claiming research or interpretability authority.

objectives.statement: Use transformer, token, context, and generation mechanisms to predict engineering consequences and design tests.

competencies.title: Model and access selection
competencies.description: Select managed, hosted, open-weight, adapted, or hybrid paths using task evidence and constraints.

objectives.statement: Compare model and access postures using representative behavior, control, cost, privacy, and lifecycle evidence.

competencies.title: Prompt and context interfaces
competencies.description: Engineer versioned instructions, messages, decoding, output schemas, validation, and context budgets.

objectives.statement: Build prompt, message, structured-output, validation, and context interfaces with explicit failure behavior.

competencies.title: Retrieval and grounding
competencies.description: Build attributable retrieval, reranking, context assembly, and empty-evidence behavior.

objectives.statement: Engineer retrieval, reranking, provenance, permission, freshness, citation, conflict, and grounding evidence.

competencies.title: Language-model evaluation
competencies.description: Construct representative cases, error taxonomies, calibrated judgments, and regression gates.

objectives.statement: Create representative evaluations, segmented judgments, error taxonomies, experiments, and release dispositions.

competencies.title: Language data and adaptation evidence
competencies.description: Build traceable data recipes, baselines, partitions, and adaptation experiments.

objectives.statement: Construct reproducible language data and adaptation evidence with provenance, separation, retention, and limitations.

competencies.title: Post-training methods
competencies.description: Select and assess supervised, parameter-efficient, preference, distillation, or continued-pretraining methods.

objectives.statement: Choose and execute the smallest justified post-training method while preserving target and protected behavior evidence.

competencies.title: Inference and operational quality
competencies.description: Connect behavior to memory, latency, throughput, capacity, cost, observability, and recovery.

objectives.statement: Qualify inference and operational behavior under workload, resource, fallback, and recovery constraints.

competencies.title: Responsible controls and authority
competencies.description: Implement technical controls without absorbing formal decision rights.

objectives.statement: Implement and test privacy, security, safety, misuse, provenance, governance, and human-authority controls.

competencies.title: Release and change
competencies.description: Release, diagnose, migrate, roll back, and learn through model-system change.

objectives.statement: Bound releases, diagnose incidents, replay evidence, migrate models and runtimes, and preserve rollback and limitations.

competencies.title: Model-system leadership
competencies.description: Set evidence standards and coordinate specialist decisions without collapsing authority.

objectives.statement: Lead model-system evidence and tradeoff decisions while preserving specialist and formal authority boundaries.
